1.headline: Retool Beats Rebuild, Cheese Children Beat Themselves
1.intro: Week 1 mostly went to form: the Win-Now Contenders (Moon Unit, Brock Hard, BateBoul, Choo Choo Crew) went a combined 3-1, and both preseason Rebuild teams (The Factory, Nikki's Victims) lost, one of them embarrassingly. But the real story of the week wasn't a Rebuild team losing, it was a Contender doing it to themselves.

games.394248955468185600-394531785582608384: This wasn't a game, it was a formality. The Factory came in with the most 2026 draft capital in the league and a roster that hasn't been built around it yet, and week 1 made the case for the rebuild louder than any scouting report could: nobody on the roster topped Bucky Irving's 16.8, starting QB Drake Maye managed 12.82, and the entire eight-man lineup combined for less than what Chicken Boys got out of Kenneth Walker (35.6) and Chris Olave (25.2) alone. Chicken Boys, for their part, got the kind of balanced production a "fallen-off dynasty" isn't supposed to have this early: Walker, Olave, Isaiah Likely (23.8) and Nico Collins (17.7) all hit mid-teens or better.
games.336348640681398272-394491025806135296: Nikki's Victims talked a big game all week and then needed 39.66 points out of Josh Allen, the league's resident handout quarterback, just to keep this from getting ugly. Strip Allen out and the rest of the roster combined for under 50 points, with Tee Higgins (7.4), Marvin Harrison (3.8) and Jayden Reed (3.5) doing essentially nothing. BateBoul didn't need the theatrics: Jahmyr Gibbs (31.1) and Jalen Hurts (28.72) did the heavy lifting before Trey McBride tacked on another 20, and this "back-to-back dominant, no championship yet" team looked like exactly that again.
games.393989477577588736-407246708687314944: Caleb Williams put up 38.26, the second-best individual score of the week by anyone, and it still wasn't close, because Moon Unit doesn't have one guy who goes off, it has four: Bijan Robinson (27.3), Trevor Lawrence (26.1), Amon-Ra St. Brown (23.7) and CeeDee Lamb (12.9) all cleared double digits. Mattpao's problem wasn't Williams, it was everyone else: Chuba Hubbard (22.2) was fine, but the next five players combined for under 33 points behind a rookie-heavy WR room (Emeka Egbuka, Rome Odunze) that isn't producing consistently yet.
games.394226654450315264-394251491289911296: This is the one to talk about. Cheese Children came into the week labeled a Contender by every preseason measure, "the deepest, most balanced roster in the league," and then somehow posted the week's low score while their own bench outscored their own starting lineup at two separate positions. Baker Mayfield started at QB and put up 11.64; Bryce Young sat on their bench and put up 36.44. Jordan Addison started at WR and scored a flat 0.0; Christian Watson sat behind him and scored 32.70. Between those two swaps alone, this team left over 61 points on the bench in a game they lost by 42.66. This is also, for the record, the same franchise that hung 167.3 on The Factory in the single biggest blowout in league history back in 2021. Nobody's questioning the roster. Somebody needs to question the lineup card. Meanwhile Fuck Michael Thomas, a preseason Rebuild team, got a legitimate breakout from rookie Ashton Jeanty (29.7) and a strong Jaxon Smith-Njigba game (25.2) and won going away without needing much from the rest.
games.390894031879553024-394253124748980224: DickTatorMiller led the entire league in scoring this week and there's a real chance nobody noticed, because a Retool team quietly posting 130 behind a 34.8-point Derrick Henry game doesn't make headlines the way a contender collapsing does. DJ Moore (21.5) and Jayden Daniels (17.66) rounded out a genuinely deep effort. Long Live Wopo got 29.96 from Lamar Jackson and 27.2 from Justin Jefferson, two stars doing exactly what they're supposed to do, and it still wasn't enough against a full lineup clicking at once.
games.1065778674277945344-394252975431766016: The week's closest game, and it played out exactly like two Win-Now Contenders beating on each other should. Zay Flowers (27.5) and David Montgomery (27.4) carried Brock Hard, while D'Andre Swift went off for 31.9 and nearly single-handedly dragged Choo Choo Crew to the upset before Jonathan Taylor's 23.6 wasn't quite enough backup.

2.headline: Terrifyingly Lucky, Federally Funded, and a Coach on the Hot Seat
2.intro: The league got its first real personality this week. The Chicken Boys are 2-0 and it should scare everybody, except the margin says otherwise. Cheese Children lost a game their own coaching staff handed away, for the second week running. Nikki's Victims are still riding federal assistance at quarterback. And somehow the two funniest standings lines belong to a 0-2 preseason Contender and a 0-2 preseason Win-Now team who can't find a way to actually win despite scoring like a middle-of-the-pack team.

games.394248955468185600-407246708687314944: This is how a 2-0 start should feel unstoppable, and instead it feels like a warning shot. Chicken Boys survived by 0.46 points, the width of a single extra point, on a week where nobody in their lineup even cracked 21: Kenneth Walker led them with 20.8, Jaylen Waddle put up 18.8, Chris Olave 18.6, and Justin Herbert only managed 10.88 at QB. Mattpao got a strong receiving day from DeVonta Smith (22.7) and a shocking 18.3 out of Jake Ferguson at tight end, but Caleb Williams gave them nothing resembling a floor start at quarterback, 8.72 points, and that gap at the position was the whole game. A "fallen-off dynasty" going 2-0 is scary on paper. Winning by less than half a point in back-to-back weeks is not the form of a juggernaut, it's the form of a team one bad Sunday from 1-1.
games.390894031879553024-394252975431766016: DickTatorMiller is quietly 2-0 and still nobody's talking about it. Travis Kelce led the way with 20.6, Derrick Henry added 16.2, Jayden Daniels chipped in 14.74 at QB, and the only sour note was DJ Moore finishing at -0.1, an actively negative fantasy performance. Brock Hard leaned entirely on Brock Purdy, who put up 29.48, more than 40 percent of the team's entire output, and got almost nothing behind him: Garrett Wilson managed 14.2, but Mike Gesicki scored a flat 0.0 at tight end and the backfield of Jacory Croskey-Merritt (5.3), David Montgomery (3.4) and Rhamondre Stevenson (3.1) combined for under 12 points. That's the week's low score, and it wasn't close to being competitive past Purdy's one big game.
games.336348640681398272-394226654450315264: The coaching staff lost this game, not the roster, for the second straight week. Bryce Young sat on the bench again and outscored the starting quarterback again, 25.08 to Baker Mayfield's 14.18, the same exact mistake as week 1 repeated verbatim. On top of that, Puka Nacua started at the dedicated WR slot and scored a flat 0.0, while Blake Corum, an RB, sat unused on the bench with 9.70 points and was flex-eligible the whole time. Just sliding Corum into the flex in place of Nacua would have been worth 9.70 points on its own, enough by itself to flip this loss into a win. James Cook (20.4) and George Kittle (17.0) had genuinely good games and none of it mattered, because between the Young/Mayfield mistake and the Nacua/Corum mistake, this team left well over 30 points unused in a game they lost by 5.64. Two weeks, two losses that were entirely self-inflicted, and the same core mistake at quarterback both times. If this were a real front office, the coach would already be fielding questions. On the other side, Nikki's Victims moved to 1-1 doing it almost entirely on Josh Allen, who put up 43.82, more than double the next-best starter, Omarion Hampton at 16.5. Tee Higgins added 12.0 and everyone else on the roster combined for under 17 points. This team is not winning games so much as collecting a federal benefits check at quarterback every Sunday and calling it a strategy.
games.394251491289911296-394491025806135296: Jaxon Smith-Njigba put up 41.0 by himself, nearly half his team's entire output, and it still wasn't enough: Jordan Love added a modest 13.8 at QB and Breece Hall 12.7, but there was nothing else behind Smith-Njigba's monster game. BateBoul got a clean, balanced week instead of one outlier: Ja'Marr Chase (23.0), Jahmyr Gibbs (20.3), Jalen Hurts (18.16) and Kyren Williams (14.7) all contributed, and that's the difference between a roster that needs a superstar game to win and one that doesn't.
games.393989477577588736-394531785582608384: The Moon Unit followed a 124.0 week 1 with 138.86 in week 2, and this time it came from two receivers going off in the same lineup: CeeDee Lamb put up 31.3 and Amon-Ra St. Brown 30.7, with Christian McCaffrey (20.6) and Stefon Diggs (19.2) adding on top of that. Through two weeks this is 262.86 points for, the most in the league by roughly 34 over second place, and right now this is the best roster in the league by a real margin, not a narrow one. The Factory, meanwhile, got a solid Tre Tucker game (24.4) and a surprising 20.0 from Dalton Schultz at tight end, and it still wasn't enough behind a 10.02-point Drake Maye start at quarterback. 0-2, and getting exactly the results a team with no real 2026 assets and a rebuild on paper should be getting.
games.1065778674277945344-394253124748980224: Choo Choo Crew is 0-2, which might be the funniest thing in the league right now, because it's not for lack of scoring. Jonathan Taylor put up 27.2, Joe Burrow 16.18 at quarterback, and the team's total of 217.24 points through two weeks is 6th in the league, dead in the middle of the pack, ahead of exactly half the other 11 teams. They just haven't found a week where it's enough: they lost by 5.94 in week 1 and by 12.22 here, both times to opponents having a good day rather than to their own bad one. This week that opponent was Long Live Wopo, who got a 36.5-point Davante Adams game and 19.0 from Dalton Kincaid at tight end. A preseason Win-Now Contender sitting at 0-2 with solidly average scoring is the most "2026 is not going to plan" storyline in the league so far.
